content.title: About
content.content: Canned bean soup is a ready‑to‑eat product that contains beans, vegetables, spices, and broth. It stores at room temperature and heats quickly, providing a nutritious and filling meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned bean soup is popular for camping and office lunches because of its long shelf life.
Beans are a good source of plant protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates.
Traditional recipes include tomatoes, carrots, onion, and spices such as bay leaf and black pepper.
In some countries bean soup is a national dish, e.g., feijoada in Brazil and bean soup in the United States.
Canning preserves most vitamins, though some vitamin C may be lost during heat processing.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans supply essential amino acids that support muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for hemoglobin formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned bean soup typically contains little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Convenient and economical
items.content: Quick preparation without the need to cook broth or chop vegetables saves time and money.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned soups often contain high levels of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bean allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Metal cans can leach trace amounts of BPA; choose products with verified safety certifications.

items.title: Thermal processing
items.content: Long‑term storage can lead to the formation of small amounts of unwanted compounds, so do not exceed the printed shelf life.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can and heat the soup on the stove or in a microwave until boiling. For extra flavor, add fresh herbs, sour cream, or grated cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer any leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 3‑4 days.
